Vous quittez le ministère après vingt he: You leave the ministry after eight in the evening. The last tram has gone; you walk home along the quay. In the hall, Mr ADLER's lamp is still on. You go to bed without dinner.
The heating works one hour in two. On the kitchen table, a letter from your sister Lena, which arrived this morning.

"My final-year placement at Hospital No. 2 is waiting for an authorisation from the Ministry of Health. I'm told it's blocked because of Dad's file. You work there now. You could ask. Just ask."
Une lettre courte. Promettre, ou seuleme: A short letter. Promise, or only reassure.
Vous écrivez trois brouillons. Le dernie: You write three drafts. The last one says: "I'll see what I can do. Don't talk about Dad to anyone." You post it downstairs, in the box in the hall.
Volume au plus bas, la couverture sur le: Volume as low as it goes, the blanket over the set.
Radio Aldria, service en langue velmirie: Radio Aldria, Velmirian-language service. The announcer reports an electricity agreement for the winter: Aldria will supply the power Power Station No. 3 no longer produces. "The Velmira authorities have not commented." Then a violin tune, and the jamming comes back.
Descendre saluer M. ADLER: Go down and greet Mr ADLER
Le gardien de l'immeuble. Sa porte est t: The building's caretaker. His door is always ajar.
M. ADLER vous offre un verre de liqueur: Mr ADLER offers you a glass of plum liqueur. "Inspector, now. Your father would be proud." He taps a school exercise book lying by the radio. "The times people come in and go out. It's my job, nothing personal. You, I always set to the right time."
Il pleut sur le District 2. Dans l'escal: It is raining on District 2. In the stairwell, someone has scratched with a nail, into the green paint, the drawing of a clock with no hands. Your father, the clockmaker, used to trace ones like it in the mist on his shop window, long ago; you no longer remember why. By morning, the building's painter will have covered it over.
Ouvrir à Vera SEDLAR: Open the door to Vera SEDLAR
On frappe. Une femme au manteau élimé, u: A knock. A woman in a threadbare coat, with a schoolteacher's satchel and a bag of groceries.
« Je suis la femme d'Anton SEDLAR. Je ne: "I am Anton SEDLAR's wife. I'm not asking you for anything, I only want to know where he is." You do not know. She puts the bag down on the doormat: potatoes. "For you. So nobody can say I came empty-handed." She goes back down without waiting for an answer. Mr ADLER saw the whole scene.
Appeler Lena depuis la cabine du hall: Call Lena from the phone box in the hall
Trois minutes, une seule pièce dans l'ap: Three minutes, a single coin in the machine.
Lena a reçu votre lettre. Elle parle vit: Lena got your letter. She talks fast: at Hospital No. 2 they are short of insulin, dressings, even syringes. "Families cross into Halvek to get them on the other side. Everyone knows." Then, more quietly: "Thank you for the authorisation. I know you'll try."
Lena décroche à la quatrième sonnerie. «: Lena picks up on the fourth ring. "Did you read my letter?" You say you haven't had time. A silence. She talks about the hospital: no more insulin, no more syringes, families crossing into Halvek to find them. The three minutes are up before she mentions the placement again.
Radio Aldria cite « une source à Halvek: Radio Aldria quotes "a source in Halvek": a Velmira worker has reportedly been arrested for smuggling medical papers for his mother. Neither the name nor the factory is given. You switch the set off before the end.
Radio Aldria parle du poste-frontière de: Radio Aldria talks about the Halvek border post: the queues are doubling, "mostly sick people and their families". An Aldrian doctor says that the Halvek-South hospital treats patients from Velmira without proper papers every week.
En coupant le poste, vous entendez un pa: As you switch off the set, you hear a step on the stairs, then the caretaker's door closing softly.
Lena est venue dîner sans prévenir, avec: Lena has come to dinner unannounced, with a loaf and two herrings. She has her hospital coat on under her overcoat. It is nine o'clock; you will not be able to do everything.
Elle parle de la commission des stages :: She talks about the placements committee: it meets on Friday. "They read your surname, they read Dad's file, they sign 'unfavourable opinion'. You, how do they read you?" She laughs, but she is waiting for an answer. Before leaving, she leaves on the table a photo of the two of you as children, in front of the station clock.
Écouter la radio d'Aldria avec Lena: Listen to Radio Aldria with Lena
Une émission littéraire. Une voix lit un: A literary programme. A voice reads a forbidden poem, "Halina", by one Teodor VARGA, "imprisoned in Velmira since 1981, and of whom we have had no news". Lena knows the last lines by heart. She murmurs them along with the radio.
Quand Lena s'en va, M. ADLER est sur le: When Lena leaves, Mr ADLER is on the landing, a bucket in his hand. He says nothing. He looks at the door of your flat, then at Lena.
Relire vos notes de la journée: Reread your notes from the day
Lena fait la vaisselle pendant que vous: Lena does the washing-up while you work.
Vous relisez le carnet du jour à la lumi: You reread the day's notebook by the kitchen light. Lena dries the plates without speaking, then leaves earlier than planned. "You look like Dad, when you do that." You do not know whether it is a reproach.
En rentrant, vous passez devant la gare: On the way home, you pass the central station. Its great clock is four minutes slow, as always. Your father used to say that a public clock running slow "has its reasons". You were nine; you had not asked which.
La commission des stages se réunit demai: The placements committee meets tomorrow morning. In your wallet you have your ministry card, with the Section 4 stamp. A phone call might be enough.
Appeler le ministère de la Santé pour Le: Call the Ministry of Health for Lena
Donner votre matricule. Ce sera noté que: Give your service number. It will be noted somewhere.
Un fonctionnaire de garde note votre mat: An official on duty notes your service number, spells your name twice. "A recommendation from Section 4? I'll pass it on." He hangs up before you have said thank you. You stand for a long time with your hand on the receiver.
Écrire à Lena que vous ne pouvez rien: Write to Lena that you can do nothing
Un inspecteur n'intervient pas pour sa f: An inspector does not intervene for his family.
« Un inspecteur ne peut pas intervenir p: "An inspector cannot intervene for his family. That's the rule, and it's a good rule." Rereading it, you recognise the sentence: it comes from circular 12/84. You post it anyway.
Forget the committee for an hour.
Radio Aldria annonce qu'une commission d: Radio Aldria announces that an international inspection commission will visit Velmira's Thermal Power Station No. 3 on 8 December, "a condition of the electricity agreement". The Ministry of Energy has not confirmed.
Le lendemain matin, votre boîte aux lett: The next morning, your letterbox has been opened. Nothing has been taken.
Dans le tram, deux miliciens parlent d'u: On the tram, two militiamen are talking about a team leader at the Power Station "who talked too much". As they get off, they look at you. They know who signed.
Au bas de l'immeuble, B. ORLIK pousse un: At the foot of the building, B. ORLIK is pushing a wheelbarrow of coal: demoted to labourer. He does not greet you. Nor does he spit.
Sous votre porte, une enveloppe sans tim: Under your door, an unstamped envelope: a coal voucher, two sacks, in the name of the district Militia. Nobody has asked you for anything. Not yet.
Vendredi. La semaine est finie ; lundi,: Friday. The week is over; on Monday, another begins. In the hall, Mr ADLER has put up the cleaning rota. Your name is underlined twice.
Elle attend au pied de l'escalier depuis: She has been waiting at the foot of the stairs for an hour. She found your address.
Elle ne pleure pas. Elle vous tend une p: She does not cry. She hands you a wedding photo: Karel BENES, young, with no scar at all. "He was a proofreader, he corrected other people's mistakes. He never wrote a poem in his life." She takes the photo back. "You signed it. Now you know what he looks like."
"Favourable opinion!" She is almost shouting. "The chairman of the committee asked whether I really was Inspector VOSK's sister. I said yes. He smiled." She starts at Hospital No. 2 on Monday. You do not tell her that, from now on, someone knows what she owes you.
« Avis défavorable. On m'envoie au dispe: "Unfavourable opinion. They're sending me to the District 9 clinic." She does not reproach you. She only asks: "Your rule, did it help you?" then she hangs up.
« Avis défavorable, dispensaire du Distr: "Unfavourable opinion, District 9 clinic." Lena's voice is flat. "You didn't answer. I thought you didn't dare. Now I think you didn't try." The line goes dead.
Partager une bouteille avec M. ADLER: Share a bottle with Mr ADLER
Il a des nouvelles du quartier. Il en a: He has news of the neighbourhood. He always does.
M. ADLER a les yeux brillants. « Au troi: Mr ADLER's eyes are shining. "On the third floor, the KOLARs, they listen to Aldria. I haven't written it down yet. We're neighbours, aren't we?" He refills your glass. You understand he is not asking your opinion: he is showing you he could do it for you too.
La boulangerie n° 12 a rouvert avec une: Bakery No. 12 has reopened with another saleswoman. The queue falls silent when you come in. The bread tastes the same; you do not finish it.
À la boulangerie n° 12, la vendeuse glis: At Bakery No. 12, the saleswoman slips an extra loaf into your string bag. "For the inspector who knows how to count." You pay for it anyway.
Deuxième semaine. Le chauffage du bloc 7: Second week. The heating in Block 7 has been cut off for good; you sleep in your coat. On the landing, the clock with no hands has been carved again, deeper this time: the painter has given up covering it.
Radio Aldria revient sur la commission i: Radio Aldria comes back to the international commission expected in Velmira on 8 December: it will inspect "the registers and the premises". The Ministry of Energy is still silent.
Les papiers que vous avez rapportés du s: The papers you brought back from basement B.
Vous relisez vos notes à la bougie. Quel: You reread your notes by candlelight. Something does not fit in the register's dates: one line seems more recent than the others. You cannot say why, and that is what keeps you awake.
Her first week in her new post.
Lena va bien à l'hôpital n° 2. Elle bais: Lena is doing well at Hospital No. 2. She lowers her voice: "A man came asking questions about you. Polite. He said he knew you." She does not remember the name. You will, soon.
Lena, au dispensaire du District 9, soig: Lena, at the District 9 clinic, treats miners. "We're short of everything. I don't hold it against you, you know." The silence that follows says the opposite.
On a glissé sous votre porte un tract de: Someone has slipped a scrap of a leaflet under your door: the cleaning rota. Underneath, in another hand, three words in pencil: "We're watching you." Mr ADLER swears it was not him.
Radio Aldria : depuis l'incident de Halv: Radio Aldria: since the Halvek incident, Velmira has been arresting "foreign agents". A correspondent speaks of neighbours denouncing each other over a light left on too late.
La cour, les fenêtres éteintes, la vôtre: The courtyard, the dark windows, yours lit.
Vous éteignez pour regarder sans être vu: You switch off to watch without being seen. Opposite, a window lights up when yours goes dark, goes dark when yours lights up again. Perhaps a coincidence. You sleep badly.
Descendre voir M. ADLER: Go down to see Mr ADLER
Sa porte est entrouverte, comme toujours: His door is ajar, as always.
« L'archiviste du sous-sol, KREMER ? Un: "The archivist in the basement, KREMER? A good man. You covered for him, I'm told." ADLER smiles. "Your father would have done the same. Clocks, archives: it's the same people who keep time and those who want to rig it."
ADLER vous ressert de la liqueur de prun: ADLER pours you more plum liqueur. "Sleeping badly? You can hear it, through the floorboards." He taps his comings-and-goings notebook. "You, I always set to the right time."
Sur un mur du District 2, quelqu'un a re: On a wall in District 2, someone has copied out two lines of VARGA in chalk. Nobody rubs them out. You reread them in passing, like a password.
Lena a laissé un mot au gardien : elle p: Lena has left a note with the caretaker: she will come by this evening. She has something "that can't be said on the phone".
She comes up the stairs at nine.
Elle sort de sa blouse une vieille envel: She takes an old envelope from her coat: your father's papers, which an elderly patient had kept "for the clockmaker who repaired her clock in 1971". There is an address, a date, a name crossed out. Lena looks at you. "You're an inspector. You can find out what happened to him."
Radio Aldria, émission littéraire : une: Radio Aldria, literary programme: a voice reads VARGA again, "of whom we still have no news". Then a statement: Aldria makes the winter electricity conditional on the visit of 8 December.
The evening routine, so as not to think.
Vous rangez, vous lavez un verre, vous r: You tidy up, you wash a glass, you wind the clock in the entrance — the one your father had set. It runs one minute fast. You do not correct it.
Ce dimanche, les cloches de Sainte-Agath: This Sunday, the bells of Saint Agatha did not ring. In the courtyard, a mother waits until nightfall for a child who sang alto.
La chorale chante sans son chef. On l'en: The choir sings without its leader. You can hear it as far as the stairwell: someone is beating time in her place, too fast.
Par la fenêtre de la paroisse, la choral: Through the parish window, the choir is rehearsing. Out of tune, timidly, but it is rehearsing. A child's voice holds the note longer than the others.
Nuit claire et froide. Dans la cour, un: Clear, cold night. In the courtyard, a child has drawn a hopscotch in chalk; the last square bears a number the rain has almost washed away: 1971.
Radio Aldria cite « une source au minist: Radio Aldria quotes "a source at the Velmira ministry": old files are reportedly being "brought into compliance" ahead of the commission. The announcer leaves the sentence hanging.
Vous écrivez tout ce que vous n'osez dir: You write down everything you dare not say: the archive, the line that is too recent, your father's crossed-out name. Then you burn the sheet in the sink and watch the smoke rise towards the air vent. Someone, somewhere, is breathing the same air.
Monter le journal à M. ADLER: Take the newspaper up to Mr ADLER
He can no longer see well enough to read in the evening.
Vous lui lisez la une. Il vous arrête :: You read him the front page. He stops you: "Your father read just like that, aloud, while winding his clocks." He hands you a small key. "If my workshop is ever shut, it's for the clock at the back. You'll know which one."
Au sous-sol, on dit que les archives de: In the basement, they say KREMER's archives have been "reorganised". Tonight, your kitchen smells of burnt paper: the wind is coming from the ministry.
Fin de l'acte : demain, une autre semain: End of the act: tomorrow, another week, darker. The corridor window on the ground floor has been bricked up, "for the winter". You can no longer see the street.
Radio Aldria annonce que la Centrale n°: Radio Aldria announces that Power Station No. 3 is "running beyond capacity" to get through the winter. An anonymous engineer speaks of missing safety parts. Then the jamming.
You and Lena, as children, in front of the clock.
La photo que Lena a laissée. Derrière vo: The photo Lena left. Behind you, the station clock shows an impossible time: the hands were painted onto the print by hand. You had never noticed. Your father was holding the camera.
« Ne montre ces papiers à personne. Pas: "Don't show those papers to anyone. Not yet." Lena promises, then: "Are you starting to talk like them, or like him?" You do not know how to answer.
La radio annonce un « renforcement des c: The radio announces "stepped-up checks" on the Halvek line. At the station ticket window, a railwayman looks at your card and hands you your change without a word.
On dit VRABEC muté aux voies de triage,: They say VRABEC has been transferred to the marshalling yards, at the other end of the country. His wife sold the sideboard at the market: you don't move house with a sideboard.
Un cheminot que vous ne connaissez pas v: A railwayman you do not know is waiting for you under the porch. He whistles three notes, touches his cap and leaves. It will take you days to recognise the tune.
Vous êtes réveillé en pleine nuit : au n: You are woken in the middle of the night: to the north, an orange glow, then a blast that rattles the windows. A minute later, the whole neighbourhood has lost power. Power Station No. 3 has exploded.
À la bougie, vous captez Radio Aldria :: By candlelight, you pick up Radio Aldria: "explosion at Velmira's Thermal Power Station No. 3, toll unknown". Velmira has announced nothing. The announcer adds: "The authorities will look for a culprit before they look for a cause."
Sans courant, sans radio, la ville muett: No power, no radio, the city mute.
You stay at the window until dawn. Lorries drive north. In the building, nobody is asleep: you hear sets switched on low, then quickly off. Fear has a sound, and it is silence.
ADLER regarde le nord par la lucarne. «: ADLER looks north through the skylight. "A factory that explodes wants a name before morning. Pray it isn't yours they ask you to write." He winds a clock in the dark, by ear.
L'appartement 7 de l'escalier D porte de: Flat 7 on staircase D bears fresh seals. The neighbours have already shared out his chairs.
PETRAS vous croise dans l'escalier D. Il: PETRAS passes you on staircase D. He hesitates, then holds the door for you. He does not know what you signed; he only knows he is still here.
L'informateur que vous avez dénoncé ne s: The informer you denounced no longer sits on the bench in the courtyard. Another has taken his place. Someone always takes the place.
Le courant est revenu par à-coups. Le bu: The power has come back in fits and starts. The official eight o'clock bulletin spoke of "the enemy within". In the courtyard, two plain-clothes men note who switches lights on and who switches them off.
Radio Aldria donne le nom : SEDLAR, Mira: Radio Aldria gives the name: SEDLAR, Mira, nineteen, "named as the Power Station saboteur". You recognise the name: you wrote it yourself today. The set falls from your hands.
Radio Aldria : à Velmira, « on tient déj: Radio Aldria: in Velmira, "they already have a culprit" for the Power Station. A woman's name is said to be going round, "a nineteen-year-old worker". Aldria has doubts: "too fast, too convenient". You think of the file you signed.
Who still dares to switch the light on.
De votre fenêtre, vous comptez : hier, t: From your window, you count: yesterday, thirty lamps in the building opposite. Tonight, six. Fear puts lights out more surely than a power cut.
L'hôpital a reçu les blessés de la Centr: The hospital has received the injured from the Power Station.
« On a reçu les brûlés cette nuit. Des o: "We got the burn victims last night. Maintenance workers, not saboteurs — people who'd been asking for safety parts for months." Lena is crying, which she never does. "Tell me you don't have to write about this."
Ce soir, l'atelier de M. ADLER, au rez-d: Tonight, Mr ADLER's workshop, on the ground floor, no longer has its door ajar.
Descendre au rez-de-chaussée: Go down to the ground floor
See what has become of Mr ADLER.
La porte d'ADLER est scellée d'une bande: ADLER's door is sealed with a stamped paper strip. Through the glass, the clocks have all stopped at different times, for want of anyone to wind them. In your pocket, the small key he gave you suddenly weighs very heavy.
La porte d'ADLER est de nouveau entrouve: ADLER's door is ajar again. He is pale, thinner, but he is winding his clocks. "You went the way you had to for them to release me. I'm not asking how." He gives you back your watch, set: it runs one minute fast.
La porte d'ADLER est fermée à clé, sa la: ADLER's door is locked, his lamp out. A neighbour whispers that "they came to take him for checks". Nobody knows for how long. You wind the hall clock yourself.
Radio Aldria : Velmira procède à des arr: Radio Aldria: Velmira is making arrests "among those around the Power Station". The 8 December commission "is maintaining its visit, under conditions". Then a violin tune, the same as on the first evening.
Chercher la pendule du fond: Look for the clock at the back
ADLER's key, if he entrusted it to you.
Vous pensez à la clé, à « la pendule du: You think of the key, of "the clock at the back". You dare not go down tonight. But you now know that your father and the old clockmaker shared more than a neighbourhood: a way of hiding things inside clocks.
The Power Station's sirens have fallen silent. The radio speaks of a "technical incident". In the tram queue, someone says aloud the name of RUDA, the dead man. Nobody silences him.
Une femme a emménagé sur votre palier, p: A woman has moved in on your landing, the door opposite. New nameplate: I. BRANDT. She leaves her door open just enough to see who goes by. She greets you by your name, which you never told her.
Without seeming to, through the spyhole.
Mme BRANDT reçoit peu, et toujours des g: Mrs BRANDT has few visitors, always people in a hurry who leave with files. Once, she meets your gaze through the spyhole — impossible, and yet she smiles. You step back.
Radio Aldria : à l'approche du 8 décembr: Radio Aldria: as 8 December approaches, Velmira is "putting its archives in order". A former official, now a refugee, testifies: "Putting things in order, over there, means making them disappear."
On the landing, impossible to avoid her.
« Inspecteur VOSK. Nous allons beaucoup: "Inspector VOSK. We are going to see a lot of each other." She does not say which service; she does not need to. You already know she is the one who keeps your file. She closes her door first.
Le témoin REIS a été vu au tribunal, sur: The witness REIS was seen in court, on the bench of reliable witnesses. He still had the eyes of someone who has been put to sleep.
On a ramené REIS chez lui en ambulance,: REIS was brought home by ambulance, "to rest". His landlady says on the stairs that he is finally sleeping.
Dernier soir de la semaine la plus noire: Last evening of the darkest week. You take out the papers Lena gave you: your father's. The address leads to ADLER's workshop. The date is March 1971.
An address, a date, a name crossed out.
Le nom barré, sous la lampe, se laisse p: Under the lamp, the crossed-out name can almost be read: an inspector, in 1971. Your father had filed a complaint — or been denounced; you cannot tell which way the arrow points. Both hypotheses frighten you equally.
Radio Aldria : la commission arrivera bi: Radio Aldria: the commission will indeed arrive on 8 December. "It will see what Velmira wants to show it," the correspondent concludes. You switch off before the violin.
Parler à Lena du nom barré: Tell Lena about the crossed-out name
Elle était trop petite, mais elle écoute: She was too young, but she listens.
« Un inspecteur, en 1971 ? » Lena blêmit: "An inspector, in 1971?" Lena turns pale. "And today, you're the inspector." She says nothing more. Before hanging up: "Be careful what you go looking for. You end up finding it."
On vous a confié l'opération MIROIR : ré: You have been entrusted with Operation MIRROR: rewriting files before 8 December. Tonight, at home, you cannot put your pen down: you are still writing, on a corner of the table, without realising it.
Radio Aldria : la commission internation: Radio Aldria: the international commission has reached the border. "It will ask to see the original files." In Velmira, the word "original" has stopped meaning anything.
Relire ce qu'on vous demande de réécrire: Reread what you are being asked to rewrite
Les dossiers MIROIR, posés sur votre tab: The MIRROR files, lying on your table.
Vous reconnaissez les noms : SEDLAR, la: You recognise the names: SEDLAR, the Power Station, and — further down the pile — a 1971 file whose heading you do not yet dare read. You are asked to turn it into another truth. Your hand trembles, not from fear: from habit.
Ouvrir à Mme BRANDT: Open the door to Mrs BRANDT
Elle frappe à votre porte, un dossier so: She knocks at your door, a file under her arm.
« Je vous apporte de la lecture pour MIR: "I've brought you some reading for MIRROR." She puts down the file, stays a second too long. "You write well, VOSK. Your father wrote well too, I'm told." She leaves before you can ask what she knows.
Lena a appelé trois fois pendant que vou: Lena called three times while you were at the ministry. The caretaker — or whoever runs his lodge now — has noted the time of each call in a notebook.
« On m'a convoquée. On m'a parlé de toi,: "They summoned me. They talked to me about you, about Dad, about 1971." Her voice trembles. "What you did for my placement, now it hangs by a thread: yours. What have you stirred up?" You cannot answer on this line.
« On est venu me poser des questions au: "They came asking questions at the clinic. About you. About Dad. I said nothing because I know nothing — that's the worst part, isn't it?" She hangs up first.
Radio Aldria : la commission a commencé: Radio Aldria: the commission has begun its visits. "For every file it asks for, it is shown a clean one." The correspondent speaks of a "country in duplicate".
The ceiling, the crack that keeps growing.
Une fissure court au plafond depuis l'ex: A crack has run across the ceiling since the explosion; every night it gains a little. You stare at it until morning. Opposite, Mrs BRANDT's window stays lit as long as yours.
Sur le palier, l'horloge sans aiguilles: On the landing, the clock with no hands carved into the paint has been covered over. Neatly, this time. The painter has left a pot of green beside your door, like a present.
On a glissé sous votre porte une copie :: A copy has been slipped under your door: your own inspection file, heading 54100, still thin. In the margin, careful handwriting has noted: "to be completed". You recognise the handwriting: Mrs BRANDT's.
54100. Your name, your dates, your times.
Tout y est : vos retards, vos écoutes de: Everything is there: your late arrivals, your radio listening, Vera SEDLAR's visit, your father's name. Only the last line has been left blank — the conclusion. As if only a signature were missing. Yours, perhaps.
Radio Aldria : la commission repartira l: Radio Aldria: the commission will leave on the evening of the 8th. "After it leaves, the refugees say, Velmira puts away its real files and brings out the fake ones." You think of the blank line in yours.
Affronter Mme BRANDT sur le palier: Confront Mrs BRANDT on the landing
Sa porte est ouverte ; elle vous attenda: Her door is open; she was waiting for you.
« Vous avez lu ? Bien. » Elle n'ôte pas: "You've read it? Good." She does not take off the security chain. "A file is always being completed. Yours like your father's. The only question, VOSK, is who holds the pen." She closes the door gently.
On vous a remis aujourd'hui le dernier d: Today you were handed MIRROR's last file: the 1971 one. Your father's. Tonight it is on your table, closed. You have been circling it for an hour.
Mars 1971. Enfin la vérité, ou son contr: March 1971. The truth at last, or its opposite.
Votre père, horloger, avait découvert qu: Your father, a clockmaker, had discovered that the State's clocks were rigged — set to run slow on the evenings of arrests, to fabricate alibis on paper. He had reported it. Eleven days later: "voluntary emigration". He never crossed a border. You are asked to rewrite that very line.
Radio Aldria, tard : un vieux musicien d: Radio Aldria, late: an old Velmira musician, a refugee, plays "the clocks' tune", the one railwaymen whistled in 1971 to tell each other that the time displayed was false. You know it without knowing where from.
La pendule du fond s'ouvre sur un double: The clock at the back opens onto a false bottom: rolled-up papers, in your father's hand, and a note from ADLER: "I was keeping them for the day a VOSK would dare to read them. That day has come, or it never will." At last you hold the proof — or your condemnation.
Dernier soir. Demain, vous signez, ou vo: Last evening. Tomorrow you sign, or you do not. The clock in the entrance — your father's — still runs one minute fast. For once, you have time to decide whether to correct it.
Le dernier soir avant la dernière signat: The last evening before the last signature.
Vous ne dormez pas. Vous rangez vos tamp: You do not sleep. You put away your stamps, your pens, out of habit. On the table, the MIRROR files are waiting. Opposite, Mrs BRANDT's light is out: for the first time, she is the one sleeping, and you the one keeping watch.
